title: Midwest surge ops micro-retro
content:
Context:
Quick handwritten micro-retrospective after the emergency priming window in the Midwest region (2029-01-14 night surge). This doc captures what we observed, a short timeline, immediate fixes, and concrete follow-ups for the coming week. Intended audience: infra ops, SRE, and platform routing owners.

Meeting: Midwest Surge micro-retro
When: 2029-01-15 09:30-10:00 PT (30m standup + 30m deep-dive optional)
Attendees: Maya Lopez (notes), Ravi Patel, Noah West, Aisha Rahman, Kenji Sato, Emma Liu (on-call)

Snapshot metrics (approx):
- Peak queued requests: ~18k (15% above our planned priming capacity)
- 95th latency for gen endpoints: 620ms -> spiked to 1.3s during eviction waves
- Error rate (5xx): baseline 0.4% -> peaked 3.2% (mostly preemption-related)
- Utilization by node class: H100 pool avg 78%, A100-p8 avg 66%, L4 burst nodes 42%
- Fallback route usage: 7% of traffic routed to low-cost variants during capacity throttle windows

Timeline & observations:
- 2029-01-14 22:10 PT: automated pre-warm (priming) kicked off for planned campaign. Priming checklist ran, but region saw unexpected spike from an ad-hoc customer test at 22:43 -> additional 8k concurrent sessions.
- 22:50 PT: preemptible instances in the H100 pool started being reclaimed by cloud provider (region-wide reclaim event). Eviction/restart churn for ~14 nodes over 18m.
- 22:58 PT: smart-router began reassigning sessions to A100 pool and low-cost L4 variants. Routing policy respected latency SLOs but increased token cost by ~12%.
- 23:05 PT: several customers observed degraded tail latency; auto-fallback triggered to hosted-small variants for long-running sessions.
- 23:22 PT: mitigation: manual bump of burst capacity + temporary increase of autoscaler target on A100 pool. This reduced queued backlog in ~8m.

Root-cause hypotheses (short):
1) Priming schedule + an uncoordinated partner test created an overlapping spike that exceeded hedging buffer. Hedging buffer we computed (20% spare) was insufficient for the simultaneous reclaim pattern.
2) Cloud provider reclaim pattern disproportionately affected H100 preemptible nodes due to provider-side policy; our node selection logic didn't favor less-eviction-prone zones during the window.
3) Cache warm-up mismatch for model variants: routing moved traffic to variants that had colder KV caches causing latency bursts at tails.

Decisions made during retro:
- Short-term: expand priming hedging buffer for Midwest windows from 20% -> 35% for the next 3 scheduled campaigns (automation change).
- Short-term: add a transient routing rule to prefer A100 capacity in zone-2 when H100 eviction odds >50% (experimental flag).
- Mid-term: introduce an eviction-resilience metric into the capacity planner (Eviction-Risk Score per node type + zone).

Immediate action items (owners & ETA):
- Maya: update priming automation to accept dynamic hedging param and run a dry-run by 2029-01-17. (ETA 2029-01-17)
- Ravi: add an eviction-risk scorer proof-of-concept to infra-sim repo; produce a heatmap for the last 90d by 2029-01-22. (ETA 2029-01-22)
- Noah: create a temporary routing flag to bias toward A100 in zone-2; rollback safe by default. Deploy to canary 2029-01-18. (ETA 2029-01-18)
- Aisha: coordinate with partner/product team that ran the ad-hoc test; request scheduling guardrails and notify them of priming windows. (ETA 2029-01-19)
- Kenji: validate KV cache pre-warm sequences for model-small and model-medium variants; add instrumentation for per-variant cold-start spikes. (ETA 2029-01-20)
- Emma (on-call): collect detailed eviction logs and attach to INFRA-2148. (ETA 2029-01-16)

Open questions / risks:
- If cloud provider reclaim events increase in frequency, current hedging by elastic spare capacity will materially increase monthly spend. Need threshold-based escalation to finance/product for budget adjustments.
- How do we reconcile cost-driven fallback (low-cost variants) with latency-sensitive customers? Need policy knob per-customer-tier.
- Are there zones in Midwest that historically show lower eviction churn? If so, can we prefer them for critical priming windows?

Notes to self / informal observations:
- We saw a curious pattern: reclaimed nodes often map to instances provisioned in the same 5-minute bucket; possible correlated behavior from provider. Add jitter to provisioning times next priming wave.
- Some canaries didn't report metrics due to a scrape config drift (prometheus job label mismatch) — Kenji to patch.

Attachments / references:
- INFRA-2148 (detailed eviction log)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-scripts/pull/332 (autoscaler adjuster + hedging param)
- Slack thread: #midwest-ops (thread ts: 1705284128.001200)

Follow-up meeting: 2029-01-18 10:00 PT (15m) to review dry-run results and canary routing flag telemetry.

Retrospective tone: short, pragmatic, prioritized. This is a micro-retro not a full postmortem; if metrics show repeat events we'll spin a full incident retro.

Hand-off checklist for next on-call rotation:
- Ensure hedging param is enabled in staging and flagged as opt-in in prod until dry-run validated.
- Confirm on-call playbook includes a single quick command for temporary A100 bias routing.
- Leave a one-line note on the #oncall-handoff doc when toggled.

END
